Behind the scenes

How this page builds itself, every single week

No reminders from mom, no new apps for the missionary. Watch a week happen:

✉️

Monday morning, a prompt lands in Jacob's inbox

One thoughtful question per week — text, audio, or video format. Mom can use our prompt library or write her own.

From: Missionary Moments → Jacob
"What's something that made you laugh this week — and what's one thing you're learning?"
🎙️

Jacob just hits reply — from his regular email

He can type a few paragraphs, attach photos, or record a voice memo or video. Nothing new to install, nothing to log into.

From: Jacob → Missionary Moments
"Ok so funny story about my first attempt at ordering pastel in Portuguese... 😂 (voice memo attached, 2:14)"
🌐

It's published here, beautifully, within minutes

The reply becomes a new entry on this page — photos in a gallery, audio in a player, plus the gentle weekly summary up top. Jacob gets a confirmation email so he knows it worked.

To: Jacob
"Your Week 34 update is live! Your family is going to love it. 💙"
📲

Everyone who loves Jacob gets a heads-up

Mom, Dad, Grandma, and anyone else on the list gets a text or email the moment a new entry posts. One link, no logins.

Week 34 · June 8, 2026Voice + Photos

The Great Pastel Incident

"What's something that made you laugh this week — and what's one thing you're learning?"

Okay so I tried to order pastéis for the district and accidentally asked for "twelve grandmothers" instead of "twelve pastries." The lady at the counter could NOT stop laughing. Lesson learned: vovó ≠ pastel. Other than that — we taught the Ferreira family twice this week and they came to church on Sunday!

🥟THE FAMOUS PASTÉIS

Week 32 · May 25, 2026Text

The week everything clicked

"Describe a moment this week when you felt like you were exactly where you should be."

Tuesday night we visited Irmã Rosa, who's been a member for 50 years. She fed us way too much food and told us stories about the missionaries who taught her in 1976. Halfway through I realized I understood every word — in Portuguese. Six months ago I couldn't order food. It hit me how much can change when you just keep showing up.
